item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I know this was written 12 years ago, but the fact that the containment procedures are:

  • So lenient
  • Such a risk to security
  • So elaborate with what she (not it) gets to the point of it being a hotel, but also
  • allowing an invisible humanoid SCP to leave the containment area

is extremely hard to ignore. On top of that, we then say that she has violent outbursts, and is an expert lockpicker. That seems like the perfect candidate to walk around the facility, what could go wrong?

Then we throw in some serious unprofessionalism on the side of Foundation personnel, to the point of warning against pregnancy? It's a glaring eyesore.

This would be deleted in nanoseconds were it to be posted today. This is in dire need of a rewrite, although I don't envy the author that has to make something compelling out of this concept, not one bit.

item.content:encoded:
I really like that she's a kleptomaniac, a ghost prankster, and possibly a murderer. Lots of personality.

I don't like the long list of things they've given her, or the warning to male staff not to have sex with her. That feels like one of those jokes about how straight men just can't resist sex with a woman no matter how bad an idea it is, and I would hope the straight men of the Foundation weren't actually that stupid.

I definitely don't like that the object class is "Euclid (With proper counseling, SCP-347 may be considered safe eventually)" — that implies that "safe" is a matter of whether or not she's well-disposed toward the Foundation, rather than an indication that sapient entities' behavior is inherently unpredictable and that living entities require regular care.

In general, it seems like they're not taking her seriously, even though apparently she's responsible for two deaths (that they know of). I like simple concepts when well-executed, but this is lacking.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
You both make good points. Thanks especially for the compae & contrast, Drewbear.

The term "x-mans" was floating around in the back of my mind as a deliberate bastardization of X-men. I thought it was from http://www.scp-wiki.net/the-big-list-of-overdone-scp-cliches , actually, but when I look at it now there's no things what are phrased that way. Guess I made it up. My mistake.

You're right that if I wrote an article like this one it would definitely not make it in, and that's the source of my confusion and frustration. I recognized that fact the moment I read it. It seems I was misguided as to the details, but this still just looks like someone took a superhero and changed them into a scip.

I mean, I could do that. Anyone could do that. And even correct the problems in tone. Picture Wolverine except he can't control when the claws come out. And he's not a rugged badass, he's just like. A telephone company service worker from Newark. He has a low tolerance for pain and nothing to live for, but he just can't DIE. Every new moon, rusty metal spikes shoot out of his arms. There's your totally unique humanoid scip. No tone problems, technically not copyright infringement, but obviously not original at all. We both know that wouldn't get in, but it's not because of tone problems or Mary Sue glorification of the SCP. I like to think it's because the SCP is obviously based on a comic book character and people who aren't even into comics instantly recognize it, but you don't say that. You say it's because of things like tone and the way she's treated.

I counter that you could change those elements and still not get in, using a premise as original as the premise of this SCP, and better craftsmanship. The fact that this already IS in, therefore becomes like a splinter in my brain. I start to wonder if anything can make my writing acceptable, short of doing it 5 years in the past.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The word you want is either X-Man or X-Men, if you meant it to be plural. :)

Now. Yes, there is a superhero called The Invisible Woman, but the term X-Man DOES NOT refer to a humanoid scip. It refers to an article written in such a way that the focus is on how awesome the scip is, and in fact focuses so much on how awesome they are that clinical tone is absent in its entirety.

That said, 347 is old. It's from before we really standardized format and tone and has a bit of X-Manning in the way she's treated and allowed to roam the facility, even as it realistically restricts her ability to do so. It steps over the X-Man line a few times, but it doesn't leap over it. It also has a touch of LOLFoundation- this is all hallmarks on old work.

It's well-written and decently done- but a lot of things got past because we hadn't established guidelines yet. The tone here is okay, but slips when it gives her brand name furniture and mentions her favorite foods. You can't get away with that anymore- don't use this as an example of anything but a well-written concept overcoming small flaws.

item.content:encoded:
I don't care much about this SCP one way or the other, but I believe the reasoning is as follows:

  • Her invisibility is always on, rather than at will like Sue Storm. She also doesn't have the ability to generate force fields.
  • Her invisibility affects her person only, rather than any clothing she may be wearing. So in order to maintain full invisibility, she has to go completely naked. It's implied that this is how she normally operates/ed.
  • She is mentally deranged due to the social isolation resulting from her invisibility. She arguably prefers being contained, as it allows her stability and social interactions that she lacked when free.

In short: her invisibility falls more on the "curse" side of the superpower spectrum, rather than the "blessing" side.
